model_annotations.Bulgarian: Figure 5 (left) illustrates the proportion of SDPA output values falling below a threshold of 1e-2 across network layers, comparing three distinct gating conditions. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the neural network. The vertical axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, indicating the fraction of output values below the specified threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a dashed black line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03,” which remains nearly flat and close to zero across all layers; a solid green line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44,” which starts near 1.0 at layer 0, decreases sharply to approximately 0.2 by layer 10, and then remains relatively stable through layer 20; and a dash-dotted blue line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33,” which begins near 0.8, declines steeply to about 0.15 by layer 10, and stays low through layer 20. All three lines are marked with small circular data points at each layer, and their average sparsity ratios are annotated directly on the plot.
model_annotations.Chinese: Figure 5(left) displays the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across network layers, comparing three different gating conditions. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” is linear and spans from 0 to 20, with major tick marks at intervals of 5. model_annotations.English: Figure 5(left) illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold of 1e-2 across different layers of a neural network, comparing three gating conditions. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the network layers. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, indicating the proportion of output values falling below the specified threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a dashed green line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03” starts near 0.98 at layer 0 and declines steeply to approximately 0.03 by layer 20; a solid blue line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44” begins near 0.0 at layer 0, rises gradually to about 0.44 by layer 20; and a dotted orange line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33” starts near 0.0, increases more sharply than the blue line, and reaches approximately 0.33 by layer 20. All lines show monotonic trends across the layer axis, with the “before gate” condition exhibiting a strong decay and the two “after gate” conditions showing gradual increases.
model_annotations.German: Figure 5(left) displays the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a threshold of 1e-2, plotted against the layer index, for three distinct gating conditions. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 20 with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the neural network layers. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, indicating the proportion of output values falling below the specified threshold. The first line, labeled “sparsity ratio before gate,” is a solid green line with circle markers; it begins at approximately 0.98 at layer 0 and decreases gradually to about 0.3 at layer 20. The second line, labeled “sparsity ratio after gate,” is a dashed blue line with square markers; it starts at approximately 0.44 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat across all layers, ending at approximately 0.44 at layer 20. The third line, labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate,” is a dotted orange line with triangle markers; it begins at approximately 0.33 at layer 0 and remains nearly constant across all layers, ending at approximately 0.33 at layer 20. The legend also indicates the average sparsity ratio for each condition: 0.93 for “before gate,” 0.44 for “after gate,” and 0.33 for “after average gate.”
